citation: Kitmitto, S., González, R., Mezzanote, J., & Chen, Y. (2018). Thinking, Doing, Talking Science: Evaluation report and executive summary. London: Education Endowment Foundation. (Independent evaluation conducted by the American Institutes for Research; ISRCTN22499525.)
report_number: EEF project: Thinking, Doing, Talking Science (effectiveness/second trial), December 2018
design: Two-arm blocked cluster randomised controlled trial; unit of assignment = School (within-region/blocked minimisation; 7 regions/blocks). 205 schools / 8,966 pupils randomised; 102 treatment + 98 control schools analysed (200 clusters); 233 Year 5 (grade equiv. US grade 4-5; registry grade band 3-6) teachers trained via a train-the-trainer model over 4 CPD days across the 2016-17 school year. Subject = primary science. Impact estimated via 3-level mixed multilevel model (pupils in schools in regions) with KS1 reading/writing and maths pretest covariates; intercept random across schools. Comparison = business-as-usual waitlist control.
problems: Single TPD arm vs one business-as-usual waitlist control (row 59). The report's own headline effect size is a model-based Hedges' g (Table 8/9, p.26): numerator = regression-adjusted school-level treatment coefficient, denominator = unadjusted pooled SD of the outcome (EEF 2018 formula). The 95% CI it reports comes from the multilevel impact model and therefore already accounts for school clustering (cluster_adjusted=true); g_se was back-computed from that CI (g_se=(upper-lower)/(2*1.95996)). Sample sizes differ across tables: 3,961 treatment / 4,055 control pupils were assessed (raw means, Table 8), but the primary KS1-adjusted impact model used 3,843 treatment / 3,963 control = 7,806 pupils (n_t/n_c recorded as the in-model sizes per Table 8 'n in model'). Design-effect ICC at the analysis stage = 0.15 (Table 4, level-2 ICC); I recorded that value (reported, not guessed). J small-sample correction is ~1.0000 at this df so g equals the reported Hedges' g. Two non-achievement secondary outcomes (pupil 'interest in science' index g=0.12, p=0.013; 'self-efficacy for science' index g=0.09, p=0.004) are pupil attitude/self-report measures, NOT academic achievement, so they were NOT extracted. Teacher-practice/teacher-survey outcomes were also skipped. The FSM result is a non-randomised subgroup (is_full_sample=false, outcome_role=subgroup) and is included only for completeness; the full-sample science contrast (g=0.01) is the primary student-achievement effect.

effect_sizes.arm_label: TDTS train-the-trainer CPD (4 CPD days, Year 5 science) vs business-as-usual waitlist control
effect_sizes.test_name: Study-delivered standardised science assessment (IEE/University of York; item bank from Russell & McGuigan 2001; raw score range 0-41), administered to all pupils at end of Year 5
effect_sizes.g_method: Report's own model-based Hedges' g (Table 8 & Table 9, p.26): d = regression-adjusted school-level treatment coefficient (adjusted difference in means = 0.08) divided by the unadjusted pooled SD of the science assessment (pooled variance 39.29 -> pooled SD 6.268), giving d = 0.08/6.268 = 0.013, reported as g = 0.01. Model = 3-level mixed model with KS1 maths and reading/writing pretest covariates. J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1) with df = 7806-2 = 0.99990, so g = J*d = reported 0.01. g_se back-computed from the report's 95% CI (-0.08, 0.10): g_se = (0.10-(-0.08))/(2*1.95996) = 0.0459; g_var = g_se^2 = 0.00211. CI is from the multilevel impact model and already accounts for school clustering.
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.5 Table 1 (Summary of impact on primary outcome); p.26 Table 8 (Primary analysis results) & Table 9 (effect size estimation); also p.30 Table 18 (compliance/CACE, same g 0.01)
effect_sizes.notes: Headline confirmatory outcome. Hedges' g = 0.01, 95% CI (-0.08, 0.10), p = 0.791 (not significant); estimated 0 additional months' progress; EEF security rating high (4/5 padlocks). Raw mean science score 19.48 (treatment) vs 19.62 (control) on a 0-41 scale; treatment pupils started with slightly lower KS1 attainment, hence the negative raw difference (-0.14) but slightly positive covariate-adjusted impact (+0.08 points). n_clusters = 102 treatment + 98 control = 200 schools; level-2 (school) ICC at analysis = 0.15 (Table 4). Additional-covariate models (Table 12, school FSM/N-teachers/region +/- pupil covariates) gave g = 0.02 (p = 0.668 / 0.635) - robustness checks, not the primary estimate. CACE/compliance estimate (Table 18) identical g = 0.01. This is the single TPD-vs-business-as-usual student science-achievement contrast for the meta-analysis.

effect_sizes.arm_label: TDTS train-the-trainer CPD vs business-as-usual control - ever-FSM-eligible pupils subgroup
effect_sizes.test_name: Study-delivered standardised science assessment (IEE/University of York; raw score range 0-41)
effect_sizes.g_method: Report's model-based Hedges' g for the ever-FSM-eligible subgroup (Table 10 & Table 11, p.27): d = regression-adjusted treatment coefficient (adjusted difference in means = 0.31) divided by the subgroup unadjusted pooled SD (pooled variance 33.86 -> pooled SD 5.819), d = 0.31/5.819 = 0.053, reported g = 0.05. g_se back-computed from reported 95% CI (-0.07, 0.18): g_se = (0.18-(-0.07))/(2*1.95996) = 0.0638; g_var = 0.00407. KS1-adjusted 3-level model on the FSM subsample.
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.5 Table 1 (Science FSM row); p.27 Table 10 (Subgroup analysis of ever FSM pupils) & Table 11 (effect size estimation)
effect_sizes.notes: NON-RANDOMISED subgroup (ever-FSM-eligible pupils only): Hedges' g = 0.05, 95% CI (-0.07, 0.18), p = 0.386 (not significant); ~1 additional month's progress; N = 2,000 pupils (1,033 treatment / 967 control). Interaction model: FSM vs non-FSM differential impact NOT significant (p = 0.330). Included only for completeness per spec; is_full_sample = false. Level-2 ICC for FSM analysis = 0.16 (Table 4). Not the primary contrast.
